title: Double-complex model for the Grothendieck spectral sequence
statement: For a composable pair $(F,G)$ as in [thm-sp-grothendieck], an object $X$, an injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$, and a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of $F(I^\bullet)$ as in [thm-sp-if-e1], the Grothendieck spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] with its abutment filtration is the spectral sequence of the first filtration of the total complex $\operatorname{Tot}G(C^{\bullet,\bullet})$ in [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. Its $E_2$-page is $E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(X))$, its abutment is identified with $R^n(G\circ F)(X)$ through $H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))$, and the left edge map of [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] is the edge map of this filtered double-complex spectral sequence, namely the quotient of the abutment $H^n=F^0H^n$ onto $F^0H^n/F^1H^n=E_\infty^{0,n}$ followed by the inclusion $E_\infty^{0,n}\subseteq E_2^{0,n}$.

proof.text: Choose the injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$ and the Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of $F(I^\bullet)$ in the construction clause of [thm-sp-grothendieck], and put $C^{p,q}:=I^{q,p}$. By [thm-sp-if-e1], $C$ is a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution in the exchanged-index convention. Transposition exchanges $d_I$ and $d_{II}$, the two filtrations of [def-sp-double-complex-total], and the first and second spectral sequences of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. The map multiplying the $(p,q)$ entry by $(-1)^{pq}$ is an isomorphism from the total complex of the transpose to the total complex of $G(I^{\bullet,\bullet})$ and preserves the filtrations. Hence the construction clause identifies the Grothendieck spectral sequence with the first-filtration spectral sequence of $\operatorname{Tot}G(C)$.

For the first filtration, [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives $E_1^{p,q}=H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})$ and $E_2^{p,q}=H^p_IH^q_{II}(D)$. By [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-properties], the vertical cycle, boundary, and cohomology objects are injective, so $H^q_{II}(G(C^{p,\bullet}))=G(H^q_{II}(C^{p,\bullet}))$, and $(H^q_{II}(C^{p,\bullet}))_p$ is an injective resolution of $H^q(F(I^\bullet))$. By [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $H^q(F(I^\bullet))=R^qF(X)$ and applying $G$ to this injective resolution gives $H^p=R^pG(R^qF(X))$.

Apply [thm-sp-if-e1] with $v=G$ and $K^\bullet=F(I^\bullet)$ to the second-filtration spectral sequence. Its $E_1^{r,s}=R^rG(F(I^s))$ is zero for $r>0$ by [def-sp-composite-acyclicity], so the only nonzero row is $r=0$: $E_1^{0,s}=G(F(I^s))$, with $d_1$ induced by the differential of $F(I^\bullet)$. Thus $E_2=E_\infty$ and $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)=E_2^{0,n}=H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))$ by the convergence clause of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. By [def-sp-left-exact-additive], this is $R^n(G\circ F)(X)$.

The image filtration in [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] has $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$, with $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}$. Hence the quotient $H^n=F^0H^n\twoheadrightarrow F^0H^n/F^1H^n=E_\infty^{0,n}$ followed by $E_\infty^{0,n}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,n}$ is the left edge map, and [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] identifies it with $R^n(G\circ F)(X)\to G(R^nF(X))$.
